questions.stem: A 10 m by 8 m rectangular field has blackberries. Peter can reach every point within 1 m of an edge. What fraction of the field can he reach?

figures.alt: 10 m by 8 m rectangle with a 1 m shaded strip all around the inside edge; the central 8 m by 6 m rectangle is unshaded.

questions.stem: Casey travels 100 miles in 3 hours including one lunch break. Her average speed while driving is 40 miles per hour. How many minutes is the break?

figures.alt: A 5-by-7 rectangular array: outer border all 1; second ring all 2; central three cells in the middle row all 3.

questions.stem: Haruki has a 24 cm wire. Which can he make, one at a time: a regular hexagon of side 5 cm, a square of area 36 cm², or a right triangle with legs 6 and 8 cm?
Two electric-bike trips total 40 miles and use respectively $\frac12$ and $\frac3{10}$ of a full battery. What is the full-charge range in miles?

What is $\dfrac{\sqrt{16\sqrt{81}}}{\sqrt{81\sqrt{16}}}$?

figures.alt: Brick-like unit-square grid with successive rows shifted half a unit; a tilted shaded square with one side spanning 3 units horizontally and 1 vertically.

questions.stem: Gold coins are 1 mm thick and silver coins 3 mm thick. How many ordered stacks have total height 8 mm?
Each identical cube has two shaded faces sharing an edge. Elijah glues cubes face to face. What is the fewest cubes needed so no shaded face is visible, regardless of rotation?

figures.alt: Two example cubes, each with two adjacent shaded faces, are glued side by side; three shaded faces remain visible.

questions.stem: Squares of sides 1, 1, 2, 3, and 5 form the shown rectangle. A curve joins a quarter-circle arc in each square. What is its length?

figures.alt: A 5-high rectangle tiled by squares of sides 5, 3, 2, 1, 1; an unbroken curve uses one quarter circle in each square, from smallest to largest.

questions.stem: Among positive four-digit integers using only even digits, what fraction are divisible by 4?
Four students in a row rearrange so no pair who sat next to each other remains adjacent. How many new seatings are possible?

figures.alt: Four students seated in a row on a bench; the first wears a pointed hat, the second glasses, the fourth a top hat.

questions.stem: In how many ways is 60 a sum of two or more consecutive positive odd integers in increasing order?
Three equally spaced integers have first-plus-second equal to 40, and second-plus-third equal to 60. What is the sum of all three?

figures.alt: Six circles on edges of a triangle: one at top, two on each sloping side, three along bottom. Moving counterclockwise from the top-left edge, sums are 9, 10, 8, 5, 4, 6.

questions.stem: Exactly 74% of the people in a poll answered yes. What is the fewest possible total number of people?

Miguel walks from a park entrance toward a tree while Luna runs to the tree and back to him. Luna runs five times as fast. What fraction of the entrance-to-tree distance has Miguel walked when they meet?

figures.alt: Park entrance at left; Miguel's arrow path heads toward a tree at right; Luna's dashed path runs to the tree and back toward Miguel.

questions.stem: An equiangular hexagon with positive integer side lengths is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side 6, with all six hexagon vertices on the triangle sides. How many distinct hexagons are there, identifying rotations and reflections?

questions.stem: Five circular coins of diameter 4 cm are arranged in two rows as shown. An elastic band is wrapped tightly around them. What is its length in cm?

figures.alt: Three tangent coins on the bottom row and two centered over the gaps, all diameter 4; band makes a rounded trapezoid around the outside.

questions.stem: Numbers 1 through 25 are split into five groups of five. Let M be the median of the five group medians. What is the least possible M?
Define $n^{!}=1!\cdot2!\cdots n!$. How many factors of $7$ occur in $51^{!}$?
